attack: The same subchart is included twice under different aliases, and the child hardcodes an object name - both instances render the identical object identity.
notes: Two rendered documents with the same (apiVersion, kind, namespace, name) cannot both exist; last-apply-wins would silently drop one. Recorded along the way: helm v4 rewrites the aliased subchart's .Chart.Name to the alias, so .Chart.Name-derived names do NOT collide - the tool defends that path; hardcoded names remain the trap.

attack: import-values pulls child chart exports into the parent values space; a value-source map that only scans the parent values.yaml cannot explain where the rendered field came from.
notes: Renders deterministically - the chart is fine. The torture target is provenance: value-source maps must attribute imported paths to the child's exports block, or say they cannot.

attack: lookup reads the live cluster at render time to fill a spec field, so a factory render cannot equal an in-cluster render.
notes: Renders deterministically offline (lookup returns empty), which is exactly the trap: the output LOOKS fine but depends on cluster state. The source scan flags lookup and routes the chart to target facts or an explicit refusal.

attack: Random generation inside spec.selector.matchLabels: every render produces a different immutable selector, so no two renders describe the same workload.
notes: The determinism gate refuses this chart before any parity claim is possible; the named route is generated-fact binding or removing randomness from identity fields.

attack: sprig env reads the rendering machine's environment variables into the output, leaking machine state and making renders machine-dependent.
detail: Error: parse error at (sprig-env-access/templates/configmap.yaml:6): function "env" not defined  Use --debug flag to render out invalid YAML Command failed: helm template torture /Users/alexis/code/helm-expt-claude-clone
notes: Helm itself removes env/expandenv from the template function map, so this fails at render with a named template error - the refusal is inherited from the tool and recorded, not silent. If a future helm re-enabled it, the environment probe would catch it as environment-dependent instead.

attack: now baked into an annotation: the rendered bytes change every run, so byte-level parity is impossible by construction.
notes: Named refusal, not silence: timestamps belong in receipts (observedAt), not in rendered objects.

attack: A values entry that tpl-renders itself recurses forever; a naive renderer hangs or crashes without a named outcome.
detail: runtime: goroutine stack exceeds 1000000000-byte limit runtime: sp=0x4afb347803a0 stack=[0x4afb34780000, 0x4afb54780000] fatal error: stack overflow  runtime stack: runtime.throw({0x105a97729?, 0x1042b63a4?}) 	runtime/pa
notes: Helm aborts the recursion with an error; the harness runs renders under a timeout so even a hang would land as a named outcome, never silence.

attack: The template branches on .Release.IsUpgrade, so the chart renders differently on install and upgrade - a single captured render is not the chart.
notes: Named class, not a refusal: both verbs render deterministically and the route is capturing both renders (install and upgrade) as separate proof artifacts.
